b0.note: Reduced rerun: rule vs XGBoost only, nozzle auto, seeds [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]. The first attempt (open, rule, XGBoost and oracle, both nozzle modes) finished 44 of 60 cells in its 15 minutes and was discarded unread.

b0_first_attempt.note: only 44 of 60 cells finished within the 15-minute cap; the partial result is not reported

verdict: Inside the simulator the learned feedback is a slightly more accurate correction than the eq. 3 rule, and LightGBM and XGBoost give the same result (their shares on target differ by less than 0.003): with the noisy reader and mismatch low + med + high, mean |true - corrected| falls by 0.12 pp [0.00, 0.22] with one nozzle per field (5.23 to 5.11 pp, against a per-card-noise floor of 4.84 pp) and by 0.13 pp [-0.03, +0.26] with free nozzles (CI includes zero). Sections on target rise by 2.1 pp [1.3, 2.9] (one nozzle) and 2.7 pp [2.1, 3.3] (free), which matches the fair oracle (gap recovery 101 % [92, 113] and 105 % [96, 119], against 48 % and 74 % for the rule). The cost is a correction that is on average 0.6 pp more negative, so more spray: volume +0.24 GPA [0.14, 0.34] (about +1 %) with one nozzle and +0.17 GPA [-0.05, +0.39] free, and with one nozzle per field drift rises by 0.36 percentage points [0.16, 0.59] (about +16 % relative, +0.80 at high mismatch) because the held nozzle can only add coverage through pressure and finer droplets; with free nozzles drift rises by only 0.02 points. With no hidden mismatch the learned correction is less accurate than no correction at all (5.11 against 5.00 pp for open loop, one nozzle) but less wrong than the rule (5.30), and its learned prior of about -2.5 pp before the first card makes it spray more than needed there. The post-hoc controls (see the section above) split the gain: against the rule shifted by the validation mean difference, 0.9 pp [0.6, 1.3] (one nozzle) and 1.7 pp [1.1, 2.3] (free) of the 2.1 and 2.7 pp remain, so roughly half of the gain on target is caution and half is information; a plain mean of the pass's card errors with the learned starting value does as well as XGBoost under mismatch (difference -0.1 pp, CI includes zero) at more drift with one nozzle (+0.09 points) and more volume with free nozzles (+0.50 GPA), and worse with no mismatch. The 5-seed b0 check points the same way on target (+1.3 pp [0.7, 2.0]) at +0.25 GPA, with no measurable accuracy gain (-0.02 pp [-0.32, +0.38]). A post-hoc adoption check over other app options (section above) finds the trained feedback no worse than the rule on target anywhere, but it over-corrects in two places: combined with the slow loop (fast_slow), where the corrections stack (total -5.3 pp) and the correction becomes less accurate than the rule's, and at c_req 40, where volume rises by 7 % and drift by 54 %.

controls.reuse: reused from the headline run (not re-run)
controls.sentences: **Reading (post-hoc, evaluation seeds).** Against a rule shifted by the validation mean difference (-0.405 pp), XGBoost still puts more sections on target under mismatch: +0.9 pp [0.6, 1.3] with one nozzle per field and +1.7 pp [1.1, 2.3] with free nozzles, that is about 45 % and 62 % of its gain over the plain rule (2.1 and 2.7 pp), with a more accurate correction (-0.19 pp in both modes, CIs exclude zero). The shifted rule is not quite as cautious as XGBoost in the closed loop (mean correction -3.00 against -3.17 pp with one nozzle, -2.90 against -3.02 free), so the share due to caution may be slightly underestimated. A plain mean of the pass's card errors with the learned starting value (-2.49 pp) does as well as XGBoost under mismatch (on target -0.1 pp [-0.4, +0.3] and [-1.2, +1.0], accuracy -0.02 and -0.04 pp, CIs include zero), but with more drift with one nozzle (XGBoost -0.09 points [-0.15, -0.04]) and more volume with free nozzles (XGBoost -0.50 GPA [-0.97, -0.04]); with no mismatch XGBoost is better than it on target (+0.7 and +1.6 pp) and in accuracy (-0.07 and -0.09 pp). Gap recovery with mismatch none is not informative: open loop and oracle differ by less than 0.5 pp there.

adoption_check.baseline: headline fast passes (rule, xgboost) at c_req 30, reused, not re-run
adoption_check.sentences:
**Reading (post-hoc, evaluation seeds, mismatch low + med + high unless noted).**

- **A, fast_slow: hurts accuracy, helps a little on target, costs spray. Flagged.** The slow loop's offset and the trained model's prior stack: total correction is -5.28 pp against -3.27 for the rule and -3.17 for plain fast with XGBoost. The correction becomes less accurate: |true - corrected| is +0.52 pp [0.11, 1.06] against the rule and +0.64 pp [0.25, 1.17] against plain fast with XGBoost. Sections on target are +1.1 pp [0.8, 1.5] against the rule, at +0.30 GPA and +0.38 drift points. Against plain fast with XGBoost the slow loop adds only +0.6 pp [0.3, 0.9] on target, for +0.28 GPA, +0.32 drift points and +0.63 s per pass. With the rule, the slow loop adds +1.5 pp at no accuracy cost (+0.01 pp).
- **B, speed control: helps.** Sections on target +4.7 pp [3.6, 5.9], volume +0.06 GPA [-0.13, +0.24], drift +0.17 points [0.11, 0.23]. With the rule, speed control lowers sections on target to 0.906 (0.930 without it); with XGBoost it stays at 0.954.
- **C, boom-height control: helps, at a small cost.** Sections on target +1.8 pp [1.2, 2.4], volume +0.17 GPA [0.09, 0.25], drift +0.16 points [0.05, 0.28].
- **D, ar1 forecaster: same as without it.** Sections on target +2.1 pp [1.3, 2.9], volume +0.23 GPA, drift +0.35 points, accuracy -0.14 pp: the baseline numbers.
- **E, c_req 20: helps.** Sections on target +4.8 pp [3.8, 5.8], volume +0.43 GPA [0.31, 0.53] (about +2 %), drift +0.23 points [0.10, 0.38].
- **E, c_req 40: on target up, but over-corrects at a large cost. Flagged.** Sections on target rise from 0.905 to 0.992 (+8.7 pp [6.7, 11.0]). The correction is 2.1 pp more negative, and it becomes less accurate: |true - corrected| +0.26 pp [0.10, 0.43]. Volume rises by 2.56 GPA [2.35, 2.77] (+7 %) and drift by 2.30 points [2.01, 2.60] (4.25 to 6.55 %, +54 % relative). With no mismatch the same pattern holds: +3.9 pp on target, +1.99 GPA, +1.57 drift points, +0.18 pp error.
- **No mismatch.** In B, C, D and E20, XGBoost is better than the rule on target (+1.4 to +4.8 pp) and in accuracy (-0.15 to -0.17 pp). Volume rises by 0 to 0.19 GPA. Drift does not change (CIs include zero), except with speed control (+0.06 points [0.02, 0.10]). In A, XGBoost is +1.5 pp on target, the accuracy difference includes zero, and volume is +0.16 GPA.
- **Never worse than the rule on target.** In no variant is XGBoost worse than the rule on sections on target. No variant raises drift or volume without some gain on target. A and c_req 40 are the two where the gain comes with a less accurate correction and a clear rise in volume and drift (+0.38 drift points in A, +2.30 at c_req 40).
